t: Founded by Aragon’s conquest of Pisan Sardinia in 1323–1324, it spent seven decades fighting the native Judicate of Arborea.
In 1720 the island and its royal title passed to the House of Savoy, which ruled the kingdom from Turin with Piedmont, Savoy and Nice.
Under Victor Emmanuel II and Cavour it led Italian unification and in 1861 became the Kingdom of Italy.
dyk: The Carta de Logu, issued by Eleonora of Arborea in the late fourteenth century, remained in force as Sardinian law until 1827, long after Arborea itself had vanished.
ev: Pope Boniface VIII grants the Kingdom of Sardinia and Corsica to James II of Aragon
Pisa cedes its Sardinian lands after the Aragonese victory at Lucocisterna
Martin the Younger defeats the Judicate of Arborea at the Battle of Sanluri
Victor Amadeus II of Savoy exchanges Sicily for Sardinia and its royal title
The Savoyard court flees French-occupied Turin for Cagliari
Charles Albert grants the Statuto Albertino and goes to war with Austria
Victory at Magenta and Solferino wins Lombardy
Victor Emmanuel II is proclaimed King of Italy in Turin

f.capital: Cagliari; from 1720 the court resided in Turin (in Cagliari again 1799–1814)
f.predecessor: Republic of Pisa; Judicate of Arborea
